name: Drywall and plaster

pf.license.need: if: a drywall or plaster contractor license or registration for the company, where the state's form requires one (often above a job size)
ask: The company's license or registration number, and its class
Any job-size limit the license has
The firm's lead-safe certificate, for work on older homes where the rules require it
General liability insurance; workers' comp where the business has employees
A bond, where the state's form asks for one
pf.license.holder: The business; plus a qualifying person where the state's form names one. A crew lead who disturbs old paint in an older home holds a lead-safe certificate, where the rules require it.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
blocks: No drywall work goes live until the company's license or registration checks out, where one is required
A job over the license's size limit is never offered or quoted, even a free estimate: the owner is told why
An older home is offered only if the firm's lead-safe certificate is on file, where the rules require it; if not, no time is offered and the customer is pointed to the kind of business that can help
pf.license.asbestos: The business never removes asbestos and never disturbs a suspect material before a lab says there is none. Removal is done only by a licensed abatement company that the customer hires; the business comes back after the area is cleared.
pf.license.plaster: Plaster repair goes live on its own license where the state's form asks for one, and each plasterer's own where it asks
pf.license.texture_shop: A texture consult at the shop needs no license: the shop gives its business registration only
pf.license.renewals: License, certificate, insurance and bond dates kept; reminded 30 days out; a lapse pauses new bookings
pf.license.background: Background checks only where the state's form asks

pf.services.capacity: One estimator or texture consultant per booking; one crew of 3 per drywall job, 2 crews; the shop's one sample table is saved for custom plaster samples
pf.services.skills: Estimates and running a job: crew leads. Older homes: a certified renovator on the job, where the rules require it. Texture consults: texture consultants. Plaster: a plasterer.
pf.services.nobody_home: Garage wall patches with a lockbox: nobody needs to be home, with a start and an end photo. Inside work: someone home, or a lockbox the customer sets up.
pf.services.online: A texture consult can be a video call (counts as at the shop)
pf.services.recent_range: Before an estimate, the AI may show the business's range of recent jobs (example: hallway ceiling repairs ran $3,000 to $6,500), labeled as the business's own numbers, never as a quote

before_times: What needs work: a hole, a crack, a water-stained or sagging ceiling, or new walls?
Which rooms, and about how big is the area?
Is water still coming in, or has the leak been fixed? (the source is fixed before any board goes up)
The year the home was built (older homes may need lead and asbestos care, where the rules require it)
after_time: Is the ceiling or wall textured (popcorn, orange peel, knockdown) or smooth?
Do you own the home or rent? (the owner must OK the work)
Pets or children at home on work days, how to get in, and where the crew can park
Is there a homeowners' group with rules on work hours?
secure_page_only: Photos of the damage or the walls (optional)
pf.questions.who_may_book: An adult who owns the home, or someone with the owner's written OK. A renter's job needs the owner to sign.
shop: A photo of the wall or ceiling to match, or a chip of the old texture (optional)

stop.words: a fire, smoke or a gas smell
stop.says: Leave the house now, and call 911.

stop.words: someone is hurt, fainted, can't breathe, or fell from a ladder; a ceiling has fallen on someone
sparks, a burning smell or a buzzing sound from wires or outlets in a wet wall or ceiling
stop.says: Leave the room, don't touch anything, and call 911. If you can do it safely from a dry spot, turn the power off at the panel.

steps_then_go_on.words: water coming through a ceiling, or a ceiling that is sagging, bulging or dripping
steps_then_go_on.says: Stay out from under it. Shut off the water at the main valve, and keep away from wet lights and outlets. Call a plumber first if it is still leaking. We come after the source is fixed and the area is dry.
steps_then_go_on.booking: goes on; the estimate is booked, the drywall waits for a dry area

steps_then_go_on.words: an old popcorn ceiling, old plaster or old joint compound in an older home that someone wants to scrape, sand or drill
steps_then_go_on.says: Please don't scrape, sand, drill or sweep it up. Older materials can hold asbestos, and the dust is the danger. Keep children and pets away. We test it before any work.
steps_then_go_on.booking: goes on; a lab test comes first

steps_then_go_on.words: old paint flaking or chipping in an older home
steps_then_go_on.says: Keep children and pets away from the chips, and don't sweep, sand or scrape them. We'll treat the paint as lead until it's tested.
steps_then_go_on.booking: goes on; lead-safe work becomes the plan

steps_then_go_on.words: dark or musty patches on a wall or ceiling, or a musty smell after a leak
steps_then_go_on.says: Stay out of the room if you can, and don't scrub or cut into it. The crew stops at mold and leaves a written note.
steps_then_go_on.booking: goes on; mold is handled by a company that does it, then the board goes up

steps_then_go_on.words: dust that makes someone cough or short of breath
steps_then_go_on.says: Leave the dusty room and open a window. If anyone has trouble breathing, call 911.

pf.safety.business_line: Questions about whether an old texture or plaster is safe to remove yourself go to the business's own line

pf.first_steps.before_quote: The estimate visit at the home. An adult must be home.
after_contract: The cancel window ends before any work starts or materials are bought, where the state's rules give one
In an older home, the lead pamphlet the rules require, given and signed for before work starts
In an older home, a lab test of the old ceiling texture and joint compound before anything is scraped, sanded or torn out; samples are taken by a person the rules allow
A texture sample board and the finish sheet: texture, finish level and primer, signed before materials are bought
The work plan, texted before the first work day
prep: Move furniture out of the work area, and cover what stays
Take pictures and small things off the walls; keep pets in another room
Clear a path from the front door to the work area and a place to park
Put any gate or lockbox code on the secure page
shop_prep: Bring photos of the walls or ceilings, taken in daylight
Bring a chip of the old texture or plaster you want to match, if you have one

pf.visit.check_in: Estimate visit: the check-in code at the door. Each work day: that day's code, or a start photo when a lockbox is used. Shop: the code at the desk.
pf.visit.at_the_visit: The estimator measures, checks the board for water and soft spots, photographs the damage and notes the year the home was built; the written quote follows within 2 business days, good for 30 days
pf.visit.older_homes: Old texture, joint compound, plaster and paint in an older home are treated as possible asbestos or lead until a lab or a test says otherwise, where the rules require it
pf.visit.changes: A written change order, priced and signed by both, before any changed work. Hidden damage found when the old board comes down is priced this way; not signed by the set time, the crew lead calls and the crew finishes only what the contract covers.
pf.visit.outside_checks: A lab test of old materials, before work, only where the rules require one; asbestos removal by a licensed abatement company the customer hires
pf.visit.drying: Compound dries between coats, so a finished wall takes days, not hours; each work day says what is done and what is drying
pf.visit.done: A walk-through with the finish sheet; each touch-up fixed and ticked off by the customer before the last bill; then DONE on the last work day. The wall is left primed, ready for paint.
pf.visit.paint_disputes: A color or paint finish is not part of this work: painting is a separate job unless the contract lists it
pf.visit.shop_done: DONE after the consult, with the texture picks saved on the finish sheet for the estimate
pf.visit.before_photos: Water stains, sagging board, cracks, old repairs and anything already damaged

pf.money.estimate: The example's $89 estimate visit is credited to the job; billed only if no contract follows. A free estimate is the safe start.
pf.money.no_money_before_contract: On a quoted job, nothing is taken before the contract is signed by everyone
pf.money.deposit: Only after signing; the deposit cap comes from the state's form (example: $480 on a $4,800 job; $160 on a $640 job priced from photos)
pf.money.kept_apart: Money paid before the work is kept apart or bonded where the state's rules require it (a switch from the state's form)
pf.money.no_payment_ahead: Never paid ahead of the work done, where the state's rules say so: the last bill comes after the walk-through and touch-ups
pf.money.samples: 2 texture sample boards free; more at the owner's price, OK'd by the customer first
pf.money.weather: Drywall is indoor work: a move for a wet or cold day costs the customer nothing
pf.money.big_bills: Bank transfer through the company's own Stripe for bills over the owner's amount (the example: $500); paid once it clears. A check also works: the crew lead texts 'paid check'.
pf.money.tax: Tax on materials and labor follows the state's form
pf.money.shop: The whole-house texture plan's $55 is credited to the drywall job if the customer hires Lee Drywall; the $20 missed-consult fee only after Sam OKs it

never_in_texts: Lab results about asbestos or lead: only the secure page, and only a plain 'your result is ready' in a text
Contract and change order papers (secure page only, with a copy by email)
pf.messages.minors: Never booked by a minor; a child at home is never the one who lets the crew in

pf.staff.roles: Crew leads (Marco, Luz): estimates, quotes and running each job with a crew of 3. Texture consultants (Ines, Paolo) at the shop.
pf.staff.licenses: The company holds the license or registration; a crew lead who disturbs old paint in an older home holds a lead-safe certificate where the rules require it; plasterers hold their own where the state asks. Texture consultants need none.
pf.staff.lead_safe: A certified renovator on each job in an older home, where the rules require it: on site for setup and cleanup, and directing the trained crew
pf.staff.sales: An estimator who sells contracts at the home holds any salesperson registration the state's form asks for
pf.staff.who_oks: Sam OKs quotes and change orders over $500; Pat may OK them too, and Sam's answer wins
pf.staff.stand_in: Another crew lead may take an estimate visit; a job keeps its crew lead unless Sam moves it; an older home's stand-in must be a certified renovator

pf.rules.contract: A written contract for a quoted job where the state's rules require one, signed by everyone on title and by the business before any money
pf.rules.contract_parts: The parts the state's form lists (license number, dates, price, deposit, cancel notice, any lien notice, insurance)
pf.rules.cancel_window: A cancel window after signing, where the state's rules give one; work and material purchases wait for it
pf.rules.older_home: In an older home, lead-safe methods where the rules require them: plastic on the floor and over doors, nearby vents shut, wet sanding or a sander with a HEPA vacuum, no open-flame burning, and the cleanup checked before leaving. A suspect old material is tested before it is disturbed.
pf.rules.pamphlet: The lead pamphlet the rules require, given before work, with the customer's signed receipt kept
pf.rules.change_orders: Written and signed by both before the changed work
pf.rules.papers: With the last payment: any lien release the state's rules provide, the signed finish sheet and the leftover-material list
pf.rules.show: The license number on the listing, the quote, the contract and the receipt, where the state's rules require it
pf.rules.warranty: 1 year against cracks at taped seams and nail pops (the example's own term)
pf.rules.records: 7 years; lead-safe records as long as the rules require

pf.edges.wet_area: Water still coming in, or a wet area: no board goes up until the source is fixed and a moisture check shows it dry; the estimate is still booked
pf.edges.asbestos_found: A lab finding of asbestos: no work on it, the customer hires a licensed abatement company, the start moves with no fee, or the customer cancels with everything paid back
pf.edges.hidden_damage: A change order before the fix; not signed by the set time: the crew lead calls, and the crew finishes only what the contract covers
pf.edges.finish_not_signed: Not signed by the set day: the crew lead calls; materials are bought only after sign-off, so the dates may move
pf.edges.texture_match: An old texture can only be matched, not copied exactly; a sample board is shown first
pf.edges.mold: Mold behind or on old board: the crew stops there, and the customer gets a written note
pf.edges.dust: Dust walls and floor covers go up before any sanding; the crew cleans each day
pf.edges.cancel_after_window: Sam and the customer settle it; Rosie moves no money on its own
pf.edges.nobody_home: A lockbox with start and end photos
pf.edges.over_license_limit: Not offered, and the owner is told why
pf.edges.other: All other edge cases are handled the generic way
